page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.3xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud instance built on x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The server supplies 12 dedicated virtual CPUs distributed across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. System memory totals 24.0 GB, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance carries no local ephemeral storage, relying entirely on network-attached volumes for data persistence. Under the KVM hypervisor, network throughput is provided with a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Integrated instruction sets include AVX, AVX-512, and AES cryptographic acceleration.

Performance testing reflects a distinction between single-threaded efficiency and parallelized processing. Benchmark results place single-core operations in lower performance tiers, seen in stress-ng single-core tests and a 1018.0 Geekbench single-core score. Conversely, multi-threaded workloads reach average tier results, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 10,201.54, 5,135.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and a throughput of 8.65 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. Small-scale model AI inference achieves 142.31 text generation tokens per second, though speed decreases significantly on larger parameter sizes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the resource layout offers moderate multi-core processing density without forcing allocations into excess RAM. Because single-thread speeds are modest and local NVMe drive arrays are omitted, this instance configuration provides balanced value for workloads that scale across vCPUs. Appropriate deployment profiles include static web serving, CI/CD software compilation, microservice backends, and distributed data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.3xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on x86_64 architecture. It provides 12 dedicated vCPUs from 6 physical cores alongside 24.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network bandwidth has a 4 Gbps baseline, and the server relies exclusively on external block storage. Benchmark metrics reveal solid multi-core performance, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 10,201.54 and 8.65 million Redis SET operations per second. Single-core performance ranks lower, creating a clear tradeoff favoring parallelized tasks over single-threaded execution. Memory bandwidth remains in the average tier for uncached 256MB operations. The server offers effective cost efficiency for workloads that utilize multi-threaded scaling, making it well-suited for web application backend hosting, continuous integration build nodes, light AI inference, and distributed data processing.
